claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.9, annual return 6%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.91 to 1.80 (change -0.10).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.91 to 1.91. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.56 (as submitted, 5 bps: 1.91); it breaks even at 32.2 bps with daily turnover 0.09.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.91 against 1.91 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 1.27 against 1.91 in research, a gap of +0.64.
The best year gives 18% of total P&L (year 8) and calm regimes give 76%; Sharpe is 2.19 in calm and 1.47 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 5 distinct specs; the best of 5 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.11, so the claimed 1.90 becomes 1.79 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.26 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.05, 95th percentile 0.45).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.91 to as low as 1.67 (as low as 1.67 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 35% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 22% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
